record.original_question: How can Lescanne's notion of well-rewrite-ordering, an extension of term embedding and simplification ordering, be extended to form the basis of a new kind of recursive path ordering?

evidence.quote: How can the notion of well-rewrite-ordering be used to as the basis for some new kind of “recursive path ordering”?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite signature of function symbols (each with fixed arity) and let $T(\Sigma, X)$ denote the set of first-order terms over $\Sigma$ and a denumerable set of variables $X$. A rewrite ordering on $T(\Sigma, X)$ is a strict partial order $>$ that is stable under contexts (if $s > t$ then $f(\ldots, s, \ldots) > f(\ldots, t, \ldots)$) and under substitutions (if $s > t$ then $s\sigma > t\sigma$). The homeomorphic embedding (term embedding) relation $\trianglerighteq_{emb}$ is the smallest rewrite ordering containing the subterm relation. A simplification ordering is a rewrite ordering containing $\trianglerighteq_{emb}$; by Kruskal's tree theorem every simplification ordering on a finite signature is well-founded.

Lescanne's notion of a well-rewrite-ordering is a strengthening/extension of these concepts: it is a rewrite (quasi-)ordering whose strict part is well-founded and that is compatible with the embedding relation, but which need not require the full simplification property and which is closed under certain natural operations used to build orderings.

Dershowitz's recursive path ordering (RPO) is constructed from a well-founded precedence $>_F$ on $\Sigma$ by the recursive definition: $s = f(s_1, \ldots, s_m) >_{rpo} t = g(t_1, \ldots, t_n)$ iff (i) some $s_i \geq_{rpo} t$, or (ii) $f >_F g$ and $s >_{rpo} t_j$ for all $j$, or (iii) $f = g$ and $\{s_1, \ldots, s_m\} \gg_{rpo} \{t_1, \ldots, t_n\}$ in the multiset extension.

Problem. Define, in a uniform manner, a new family of recursive-path-style orderings on $T(\Sigma, X)$ whose construction is based on an arbitrary given well-rewrite-ordering (in Lescanne's sense) in place of, or in addition to, a precedence on function symbols, in such a way that:

(a) The resulting relation is itself a well-rewrite-ordering on $T(\Sigma, X)$;
(b) When the input well-rewrite-ordering is taken to be the empty ordering (with a precedence on $\Sigma$ supplied separately), the construction specializes to Dershowitz's recursive path ordering;
(c) The construction is closed under the natural lifting operations (multiset and lexicographic status on argument tuples) and yields a strictly larger class of well-founded rewrite orderings than RPO, capable of orienting rewrite systems that no RPO with any precedence can orient.

Give such a definition and prove (a)–(c), or show that no such construction exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface Lescanne's and Jouannaud–Lescanne's work on recursive decomposition ordering and various RPO extensions (lexicographic status, AC-RPO, higher-order LPO, infinite labelled systems), but no source explicitly reports a recursive-path-ordering construction built directly on Lescanne's well-rewrite-orderings, nor a proof that this is impossible. The status of this specific question is unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Recursive Decomposition Ordering
status_evidence.snippet: Jouannaud and Lescanne introduced the recursive decomposition ordering, a simplification ordering containing Dershowitz's RPO.
status_evidence.claim: Related extensions of RPO by Lescanne exist, but none addresses well-rewrite-orderings explicitly.

status_evidence.title: Path ordering (term rewriting) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of RPO and its variants; no mention of a construction based on Lescanne's well-rewrite-orderings.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on path orderings do not record a resolution of this question.
